title: Great Hypostyle Hall
summary: An immense columned hall built between the Second and Third Pylons, with unusually rich evidence of changing decoration and royal interventions.
orientation: On the main east–west axis, east of the Second Pylon and west of the Third Pylon.

periods.date: Late 14th / early 13th century BCE (approximate; chronology dependent)
periods.role: Major construction and raised-relief decoration of the northern wing.
Completed much of the southern decoration, largely in sunk relief; altered selected earlier inscriptions.

architecture: Twelve taller open-papyrus-capital columns mark the central nave.
122 shorter closed-bud papyrus columns occupy the flanking wings.
The higher central nave allowed clerestory lighting above the lower flanking roof levels.
lookFor: Contrast open and closed papyrus capitals.
Compare northern raised relief with southern sunk relief; note that later reworking complicates simple attribution.
Look for royal names and traces of re-cutting rather than assuming every cartouche is original to its surrounding relief.
interpretation: The hall can be read both as a ritual architectural space and as a layered historical document recording construction, succession and later interventions.
caveats: Not every individual relief can be securely attributed by technique alone.
Precise standing positions, condition and current access are not yet field-verified.
